#load in dates properly

```{r}
dates <- as.Date(unique(survival$date))

dates <- c(as.POSIXct("2025-06-27"), dates)

dates <- as.Date(dates)

```


```{r}

# need to filter so that low tide ones stay when immersed, high tides stay when immersed
do_current_2 <- do_current %>%
  filter((tide.x== "H" & up_Immersed == "Y")| (tide.x== "L" & low_Immersed == "Y")) %>%
  group_by(as.Date(datetime), bag.x) %>%
  mutate(daily_min = min(DO_adj, na.rm = TRUE),
         date = as.Date(datetime))

do_current_2$interval <- cut(do_current_2$date, breaks = dates, labels = as.character(dates[-1]))

do_current_3 <- do_current_2%>%
  filter(!is.na(interval)) %>%
  group_by(bag.x, interval) %>%
  summarise(avg_DO_min = mean(daily_min))

survival$bag <- substr(survival$bag_num, 1, 2)

do_current_3$interval<- as.Date(do_current_3$interval)
survival$bag <- as.factor(survival$bag)
do_current_3$bag <- as.factor(do_current_3$bag.x)

survival_2 <- left_join(survival, do_current_3, join_by("date" == "interval", "bag" == "bag"))
```

# cox modeling
```{r}
## ============================================================
## Reformatting interval-censored, grouped bag-level survival
## counts into person-period (counting process) format for coxph()
## ============================================================
##
## ASSUMPTIONS YOU NEED TO CHECK / EDIT:
## 1. `date` is the CHECK date (end of an interval), and each bag_num
##    has multiple rows, one per check date, in chronological order.
## 2. Deployment / study-start date. The code below uses each bag's
##    *first observed date* as day 0. If oysters were actually
##    deployed earlier than the first check (i.e. the first `dead`
##    count already reflects a real elapsed interval), replace
##    `min(date)` below with your true deployment date.
## 3. `alive_num` = number alive at the END of that row's interval,
##    `dead` = number that died DURING that row's interval,
##    `init_live_ImageJ` = number alive at the very start (bag deployment).
## 4. Bag-level covariates (density, tide, piling, rack, top_bottom)
##    are constant across a bag's rows; avg_DO_min / avg_temp_max
##    vary by interval (time-varying).
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: expand each bag's interval counts into person-period rows
# --------------------------------------------------------------
expand_to_person_period <- function(df) {

  df <- df %>% arrange(bag_num, date)
  bags <- split(df, df$bag_num)

  out <- map_dfr(bags, function(b) {
    b <- b %>% arrange(date)

    n_init    <- b$init_live_ImageJ[1]
    alive_ids <- seq_len(n_init)           # pseudo-individual IDs, 1..n_init

    # IMPORTANT: all bags were deployed on the SAME calendar date, which
    # is ~2 weeks BEFORE the survival dataset's first recorded check.
    # Day 0 must be the true deployment date, not the first observed
    # date -- otherwise the ~2 weeks of at-risk time (and any deaths
    # that occurred in it, reflected in the first row's `dead` count)
    # get silently dropped, inflating the apparent hazard in interval 1.
    ref_date <- as.Date("2025-06-24")   # deployment date, confirmed by user

    # t = 0 is the deployment date itself. The loop below computes each
    # row's t_stop from ref_date, so the FIRST interval naturally runs
    # from 0 (deployment) to however many days elapsed to the first
    # checkpoint -- t_prev must start at 0, not at the first checkpoint's
    # elapsed time (setting it to the latter collapses interval 1 to
    # zero length, which is why deaths were all landing on the
    # checkpoint day: runif(min=x, max=x) just returns x).
    t_prev <- 0

    first_gap <- as.numeric(difftime(min(b$date), ref_date, units = "days"))
    if (first_gap < 0) {
      stop("First observed date is before the deployment date -- check ref_date.")
    }

    rows <- list()

    for (i in seq_len(nrow(b))) {

      t_start <- t_prev
      t_stop  <- as.numeric(difftime(b$date[i], ref_date, units = "days"))
      n_dead  <- b$dead[i]

      # guard against count mismatches
      n_dead <- min(n_dead, length(alive_ids))

      dead_ids    <- if (n_dead > 0) alive_ids[seq_len(n_dead)] else integer(0)
      survive_ids <- setdiff(alive_ids, dead_ids)

      make_rows <- function(ids, event, stop_time) {
        if (length(ids) == 0) return(NULL)
        tibble(
          bag_num      = b$bag_num[i],
          id           = ids,
          tstart       = t_start,
          tstop        = stop_time,
          event        = event,
          avg_DO_min   = b$avg_DO_min[i],
          avg_temp_max = b$avg_temp_max[i],
          density      = b$density[i],
          tide         = b$tide[i],
          piling       = b$piling[i],
          rack         = b$rack[i],
          top_bottom   = b$top_bottom[i]
        )
      }

      # --- interval-censoring imputation (per Pernet-style approach) ---
      # Instead of pinning deaths to the END of the interval, randomly
      # assign each death a day uniformly within (t_start, t_stop].
      # This avoids artificially stacking all deaths at interval
      # boundaries, which can bias hazard estimates and residual checks.
      if (length(dead_ids) > 0) {
        death_times <- runif(length(dead_ids), min = t_start, max = t_stop)
        # guard against a random draw landing exactly on t_start
        death_times <- pmax(death_times, t_start + 1e-6)
        for (k in seq_along(dead_ids)) {
          rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- make_rows(dead_ids[k], 1, death_times[k])
        }
      }

      # survivors: censored (event = 0) if this is the bag's last row,
      # otherwise they simply carry forward into the next interval
      # (still get an event = 0 row for THIS interval, since covariates
      # were in effect during it, running to the full interval end)
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- make_rows(survive_ids, 0, t_stop)

      alive_ids <- survive_ids
      t_prev    <- t_stop
    }

    bind_rows(rows)
  })

  out %>%
    mutate(subject_id = paste(bag_num, id, sep = "_")) %>%
    filter(tstop > tstart)   # drop any zero-length intervals
}

survival_long <- expand_to_person_period(survival_3)
survival_long_summer <- survival_long %>%
  filter(tstop <= 83)

survival_long_summer2 <- survival_long_summer %>%
  mutate(tide = case_when(
    tide == "H"  ~ 0.826,
    tide == "L" ~ 0)) %>%
  mutate(density = case_when(
    density == "D" ~ 300,
    density == "S" ~ 150
  ))


# --------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: fit the Cox model (counting-process form, time-dependent
# covariates) -- this is the "model 3" structure in the paper:
# left-truncated, right-censored Cox with time-varying environmental
# covariates, oysters within a bag treated as a cluster for robust SEs.
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE: set.seed() before expand_to_person_period() if you want the
# random death-day imputation to be reproducible. Since the imputation
# is stochastic, it's good practice to refit across several random
# draws (e.g. 10-20) and check that coefficient estimates/p-values are
# stable -- this is effectively single imputation vs. the "assign once
# and check robustness" approach many interval-censored studies use.



cox_model3 <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ avg_DO_min + avg_temp_max +
    density + tide + piling + rack + top_bottom + cluster(bag_num),
  data    = survival_long_summer2,
  ties    = "efron"
)
summary(cox_model3)
#
# ## Univariate screening first (as in the paper), THEN build the
# ## multivariate model from significant terms via stepwise selection:
cox_univ_temp <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ avg_temp_max +
                          cluster(bag_num), data = survival_long_summer2)
summary(cox_univ_temp)
cox_univ_DO   <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ avg_DO_min +
                          cluster(bag_num), data = survival_long_summer2)
summary(cox_univ_DO)
# # ... etc. for each candidate covariate, then combine the significant
# # ones into cox_model3 above (drop non-significant terms one at a time,
# # e.g. via step() -- note step() ignores cluster(); refit with
# # cluster() once the final term set is chosen).
#
# ## Check the proportional hazards assumption (paper used Martingale
# ## residuals; cox.zph is the standard equivalent using scaled
# ## Schoenfeld residuals, and is the modern default check in R):
ph_check <- cox.zph(cox_model3)
print(ph_check)
plot(ph_check)   # look for trends in residuals vs. time -> PH violation
#
# ## If PH is violated for a factor (e.g. an age-class or origin
# ## variable), stratify by it instead of including it as a covariate
# ## (this lets the baseline hazard differ by stratum while still
# ## sharing the other coefficients):
# # cox_model3_strat <- coxph(
# #   Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ avg_DO_min + avg_temp_max +
# #     density + tide + piling + rack + strata(top_bottom) +
# #     cluster(bag_num),
# #   data = survival_long
# # )

```

# path analysis 
```{r}

# ================================================================
# STEP 4: FULL PATH ANALYSIS (piecewise / local-estimation SEM)
#
# DAG being tested:
#   density -> DO, density -> temp, density -> survival (direct)
#   tide    -> DO, tide    -> temp
#   piling  -> temp
#   rack    -> DO
#   DO -> survival, temp -> survival
#
# Cox models with time-varying covariates aren't supported by lavaan
# or most all-in-one SEM engines, so this uses PIECEWISE estimation
# (Shipley's approach): fit one regression per node, using only that
# node's direct parents as predictors, then combine coefficients for
# indirect/total effects and test omitted edges via d-separation.
#
# NOTE: the `piecewiseSEM` package automates this (and gives a Fisher's
# C global goodness-of-fit test), but its coxph support is inconsistent
# across versions -- check `?piecewiseSEM::psem` for your version before
# relying on it. The manual version below always works and makes every
# step explicit, which is worth doing at least once regardless.
# ================================================================
 

bag_interval <- survival_3 %>%
  distinct(bag_num, date, density, avg_temp_max, avg_DO_min, tide, piling, rack, top_bottom)

bag_interval_summ <- bag_interval %>%
  filter(date <= "2025-09-15")

str(bag_interval_summ$date)

bag_interval_summ <- bag_interval_summ %>%
  mutate(tide = case_when(
    tide == "H"  ~ 0.826,
    tide == "L" ~ 0)) %>%
  mutate(density = case_when(
    density == "D" ~ 300,
    density == "S" ~ 150
  ))



bag_interval_summ$date <- as.Date(bag_interval_summ$date )
## --- local model 1: DO's parents are density, tide, rack ---
DO_mod <- lmer(avg_DO_min ~ density + tide + rack +
                  (1 | date) + (1 | bag_num),
                data = bag_interval_summ)
summary(DO_mod)
 
## --- local model 2: temp's parents are density, tide, piling ---
temp_mod <- lmer(avg_temp_max ~ density + tide + piling +
                    (1 | date) + (1 | bag_num),
                  data = bag_interval_summ)
summary(temp_mod)

## --- local model 3: survival's parents are density (direct), DO, temp ---
## tide/piling/rack deliberately excluded -- your DAG says they act
## ONLY through DO/temp, not directly on survival


cox_path <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ density + avg_DO_min + avg_temp_max +
    cluster(bag_num),
  data = survival_long_summer2
)
summary(cox_path)

## --- d-separation checks: are tide/piling/rack REALLY only acting
## through DO/temp, or do they have a leftover direct effect? ---
## Add each back into the survival model one at a time; if it's
## non-significant, that supports the "no direct edge" assumption.
cox_dsep_tide <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ density + avg_DO_min + avg_temp_max +
    tide + cluster(bag_num),
  data = survival_long_summer2
)
summary(cox_dsep_tide)   # check p-value on `tide`

cox_dsep_piling <- update(cox_path, . ~ . + piling)
summary(cox_dsep_piling)  # check p-value on `piling`
#
cox_dsep_rack <- update(cox_path, . ~ . + rack)
summary(cox_dsep_rack)    # check p-value on `rack`
## If any of these come in significant, your DAG is missing an edge --
## add it (e.g. piling -> survival directly, perhaps wave/physical
## exposure rather than a temperature-mediated effect) and refit.
 
## --- ASSEMBLING DIRECT/INDRECT TOTAL EFFECTS  ---
## Standardizing continuous predictors first makes path coefficients
## comparable in magnitude (otherwise a 1-unit change means something
## different for density vs. temp vs. DO). Do this on a COPY of the
## data used for the local models, not on survival_long time columns.
#

# compute standardization constants ONCE, from bag-interval-level data
# (not separately per table -- survival_long has duplicated rows per
# bag-interval, which would shift the mean/sd used there)
dens_mean <- mean(bag_interval_summ$density); dens_sd <- sd(bag_interval_summ$density)
tide_mean <- mean(bag_interval_summ$tide);    tide_sd <- sd(bag_interval_summ$tide)
DO_mean   <- mean(bag_interval_summ$avg_DO_min);   DO_sd   <- sd(bag_interval_summ$avg_DO_min)
temp_mean <- mean(bag_interval_summ$avg_temp_max, na.rm = TRUE); temp_sd <- sd(bag_interval_summ$avg_temp_max, na.rm = TRUE)

# mutating and standardizing the environmental data
bag_interval_z <- bag_interval_summ %>%
  mutate(
    density = (density - dens_mean) / dens_sd,
    tide    = (tide - tide_mean) / tide_sd,
    position = factor(top_bottom,
                            levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                            labels = c("single", "dense_bottom", "dense_top")),
                      bag = sub("-.*", "", bag_num))
  


DO_interval_z <- bag_interval_z %>%
  distinct(bag, date, avg_DO_min, density, tide, rack)

# mutating and standardizing survival data
survival_long_z <- survival_long_summer2 %>%
  mutate(
    density      = (density - dens_mean) / dens_sd,
    tide         = (tide - tide_mean) / tide_sd,
    avg_DO_min   = (avg_DO_min - DO_mean) / DO_sd,
    avg_temp_max = (avg_temp_max - temp_mean) / temp_sd,
    bag = sub("-.*", "", bag_num),
    position = factor(top_bottom,
                            levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                            labels = c("single", "dense_bottom", "dense_top"))
  )

# DO model
DO_mod <- lmerTest::lmer(avg_DO_min ~ density + tide + rack + (1 | date) + (1 | bag), data = DO_interval_z)
summary(DO_mod, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")

# Temp model
temp_mod <- lmerTest::lmer(avg_temp_max ~ position + tide + piling + (1 | date) + (1 | bag), data = bag_interval_z)
summary(temp_mod, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")
library(emmeans)
emmeans(temp_mod, pairwise ~ position, adjust = "tukey")

# Cox model 
cox_path <- coxph(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ avg_DO_min + avg_temp_max + cluster(bag),
  data = survival_long_z
)
summary(cox_path)
library(car)
vif(cox_path)

survival_long_z %>%
  filter(is.na(avg_DO_min) | is.na(avg_temp_max) | is.na(tide))

# frailty model
# cox_frailty2 <- coxme(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ position + tide + avg_DO_min + avg_temp_max +
#                          (1 | bag), data = survival_long_z)
# summary(cox_frailty2)
# 
# names(fixef(DO_mod))

#Extracting coefficients
a_DO_density           <- fixef(DO_mod)[["density"]]
a_DO_tide               <- fixef(DO_mod)[["tide"]]
a_temp_position_bottom  <- fixef(temp_mod)[["positiondense_bottom"]]
a_temp_position_top     <- fixef(temp_mod)[["positiondense_top"]]
a_temp_tide              <- fixef(temp_mod)[["tide"]]

b_DO     <- coef(cox_path)["avg_DO_min"]
b_temp   <- coef(cox_path)["avg_temp_max"]
# c_direct_bottom <- coef(cox_path)["positiondense_bottom"]
# c_direct_top    <- coef(cox_path)["positiondense_top"]
# d_tide_direct   <- coef(cox_path)["tide"]

# Getting total effects
indirect_bottom_via_temp <- a_temp_position_bottom * b_temp
indirect_top_via_temp    <- a_temp_position_top * b_temp
indirect_via_DO          <- a_DO_density * b_DO   # same for both layers -- DO isn't layer-resolved

# Total effect 
total_bottom_effect <- indirect_bottom_via_temp + indirect_via_DO
total_top_effect    <- indirect_top_via_temp + indirect_via_DO
total_tide_effect   <- (a_DO_tide * b_DO) + (a_temp_tide * b_temp)

# Data frame with effects
tibble(
  path = c( "dense_bottom -> temp -> mortality ",
           "density -> DO -> mortality (shared across layers)", "TOTAL dense_bottom effect",
            "dense_top -> temp -> mortality",
           "TOTAL dense_top effect",
            "tide -> DO -> mortality", "tide -> temp -> mortality",
           "TOTAL tide effect"),
  coefficient = c(indirect_bottom_via_temp, indirect_via_DO,
                  total_bottom_effect, indirect_top_via_temp,
                  total_top_effect,
                  a_DO_tide * b_DO, a_temp_tide * b_temp,
                  total_tide_effect)
)


ph_check <- cox.zph(cox_path )
print(ph_check)
plot(ph_check)   

#

```


#Bootstrapping CI's
```{r}
## Bootstrap CIs on each indirect/total effect using the same
## bag-resampling approach as the STEP 3 mediation section above --
## product-of-coefficients terms are not normally distributed, so
## don't rely on Wald SEs from the individual models for these.

library(boot)

unique_bags <- unique(survival_long_z$bag)   # resample at the PHYSICAL bag level

boot_coefs <- function(all_bags, indices) {
  sampled_bags <- all_bags[indices]

  # rebuild the dataset, allowing bags to repeat if drawn more than once
  d_surv <- map_dfr(seq_along(sampled_bags), function(i) {
    survival_long_z %>%
      filter(bag == sampled_bags[i]) %>%
      mutate(bag = paste0(bag, "_rep", i))   # relabel so repeated bags aren't treated as one cluster
  })

  fit <- tryCatch(
    coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ avg_DO_min + avg_temp_max +
            cluster(bag), data = d_surv),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(fit)) return(rep(NA, 4))

  coef(fit)[c("avg_DO_min", "avg_temp_max")]
  # add "avg_temp_max" too if you want all five in one call -- boot() output
  # index order will follow whatever order you list here
}

set.seed(123)
boot_out <- boot(data = unique_bags, statistic = boot_coefs, R = 2000)

# check how many resamples actually succeeded
sum(!is.na(boot_out$t[,1]))

# CIs for each coefficient (index order matches the c(...)/[...] above)
boot.ci(boot_out, type = "perc", index = 1)   # positiondense_bottom
boot.ci(boot_out, type = "perc", index = 2)   # positiondense_top
boot.ci(boot_out, type = "perc", index = 3)   # tide
boot.ci(boot_out, type = "perc", index = 4)   # avg_DO_min

# tidy summary of all bootstrapped estimates vs. original model
data.frame(
  term = c("avg_DO_min", "avg_temp_max"),
  original_coef = coef(cox_path)[c("avg_DO_min", "avg_temp_max")],
  boot_mean = colMeans(boot_out$t, na.rm = TRUE),
  boot_se   = apply(boot_out$t, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```
